messages:
Alex (Support): Customer (Acme) opened a P1 — sudden rise in 5xx and auth errors after 08:12 UTC. They saw traffic routed to eu-central and latencies spiked 200-500ms. Can we confirm a failover?
Dave (Eng-oncall): Looking. Any request ids / example timestamps?
Alex (Support): Sent a few in the ticket: req=rc_7e8a2 at 2026-02-25T08:13:10Z, req=rc_7e8a8 08:13:37Z. Customer pasted this error from their client: "token signature invalid" and long TLS handshake times when hitting eu.
Carla (Eng-SRE): I can see an automatic region failover around 2026-02-25T08:12:55Z for that org. Health aggregator marked us-east as unhealthy due to repeated healthcheck timeouts from the probe cluster.
Ben (Netops): There were a few NLB config changes pushed yesterday to us-east (keepalive/window tuning). Could be related. Any probe logs?
Alex (Support): Attached typical repro curl from customer: 
``
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <user-token>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/encode -w '
INFO: %{time_total}s' -o /dev/null
```
They said the same token works if they force us-east via --resolve.
Dave (Eng-oncall): That matches a routing-failover not an auth backend bug. But token validation failing in eu is odd — our token verification is global. Could be KMS key unavailability or a clock skew. Carla, can you pull healthcheck and auth service logs around that window?
Carla (Eng-SRE): Pulling: health-probe/us-east shows 3x 504s between 08:12:50-08:12:56 from probe-ip 34.210.12.9. Probe logs: 
``
[08:12:50] probe->api: TLS handshake timeout
[08:12:52] probe->api: connection reset by peer
[08:12:55] probe->api: upstream read timeout
```
But our api-ingress metrics show steady pod count and no pod restarts.
Ben (Netops): I also see a partial firewall rule rollback on the edge ACLs at 08:11:30 (auto-roll back failed). There was a brief mis-applied rule that dropped connections from the probe CIDR for ~40s. That explains health timeouts.
Alex (Support): So probes dropped -> failover to eu -> cross-region latency. But why token signature errors?
Dave (Eng-oncall): Two hypotheses: 1) Short-lived service tokens signed by region-specific KMS key that hadn't been replicated yet, 2) Our routing changed headers (x-region) and the client library rejects tokens with region claim mismatch. Need evidence.
Carla (Eng-SRE): Checking auth logs from eu-central at 08:13:10 (req rc_7e8a2): auth-service reports "signature verification failed: key not found" for the kid in the JWT header. The kid exists in us-east keystore. Replication lag shows a 6s delay — but the probe outage was ~40s so some requests hit eu before keystore had the key.
Ben (Netops): TL;DR: firewall mishap caused probe drop -> failover -> some requests ended up at eu where JWKs weren't yet replicated -> signature errors and elevated latency.
Alex (Support): Customer impact summary for ticket: traffic failover to eu resulted in increased p99 latency and intermittent auth validation failures. They saw ~5% error rate for ~2 minutes.
Dave (Eng-oncall): Immediate actions: 1) Re-enable the proper ACL and verify probes reach us-east (Ben). 2) Add quick mitigation: allow fallback routing to prefer previous region for sessions until keystore replication confirmed (Carla/Infra). 3) Postmortem and customer communication (Alex).
Ben (Netops): ACL rollback completed at 08:14:10 and probes returned healthy by 08:14:22. I can share the diff that caused the problem.
Carla (Eng-SRE): Hold-open mitigation: adding a transient policy to avoid routing existing sessions cross-region for 120s after failover. I'll draft the change, but want ops review. Also adding metric to alert if keystore replication lag > 3s during any failover.
Dave (Eng-oncall): Good. Can someone paste a minimal repro to show how to force-route and confirm token works vs fails? Alex?
Alex (Support): Repro steps customer used: 1) Acquire token against us-east (normal flow). 2) Force-route to eu by changing DNS to point to eu LB and call same token: it fails with "signature invalid". They then forced --resolve to us-east and token worked. I'll paste exact curl and sample headers in the ticket.
Carla (Eng-SRE): From post-incident quick fix: we hotpatched keystore replication to prioritize KMS key material for signed tokens (rollout completed at 08:20). No further signature errors seen after 08:21 per logs.
infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0225-14 and assigned to eng-sre.
Alex (Support): I'll update the customer with timeline and mitigation. Thanks all. :v:
Dave (Eng-oncall): Follow-ups: - Ben to share ACL diff - Carla to PR transient session-routing policy + replication alert - Alex to send customer summary. We'll schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow.
Carla (Eng-SRE): Noted. I'll attach logs and sample traces to the incident.
Ben (Netops): Diff posted: ACL change accidentally excluded probe CIDR due to inverted rule ordering. Oops.
Alex (Support): Closing loop with customer in ticket, marking as resolved on our side, pending PM postmortem notes.
